rules.banned_because: Someone else's names, kept out of everything Euphonia publishes (Appendix E; setting/ip-review.md).
rules.fey_type_because: "Fey" survives only as the creature type; the setting's prose says "fae" (Book Two, What's Different). The 2024 rules' own names keep it too: Fey Ancestry, Fey Touched, Fey Wanderer, Summon Fey and the SRD's Conjure Fey (Chat, 15 November).

regions.intro: The setting's own people here: where a party meets them, what they want and how a table uses them. Each has a pregen sheet except Sister Ondine.

people.name: Ser Marin Zorzi
people.text: One of Venice's three State Inquisitors, a tiefling of an old patrician house who has worn a plain white mask in court since his horns came in. You meet him only in the Ten's windowless court room, or by posting a denunciation in a lion's mouth: he reads them himself at night and can tell spite from fear by the handwriting. He wants, once, to see the face of the halfling whose file he has read more often than his breviary. The Venice Job's villain, or its most dangerous patron; the brass figure at his elbow turns its head when you lie.

people.name: Zanetta Bon
people.text: A halfling carnival masker of the Giudecca who forged health passes, went into the Hidden and came home able to fold space. Find her masked in a bauta at the Ridotto's faro table in Carnival, losing small sums to a sergeant of the Ten's men. She wants her own file out of the Ten's archive, to read what they think she is. The Venice Job's way in and its way out, and the Crossing Danae on Venice's rooftops; what she owes the Hidden for the doors, she keeps to herself.

people.name: Simon Horowitz
people.text: The ghetto's Kabbalist (see Running Euphonia, Notable People), eleven pages into the book the archangel Michael gave him and after the twelfth. He works past midnight at a borrowed table at the back of a study house, by a candle-end, and trusts no one who promises anything. A contact or teacher: the Venice Job's way into the ghetto, its reader of the scryers' hand and the one who knows the golem's word.

people.name: Matthias Kessler
people.text: A taster and apothecary's man at the Habsburg court in Vienna, paid to keep his masters alive, and by some of them for the other thing. Find him in the kitchens under the Hofburg at the dinner hour, gloves folded beside the dishes he has just tasted; the scullery boys love him, and witnesses afterward can't describe his face. A Hollowed Counsellor who wants to keep the one thing he kept from before, and to keep anyone from knowing what it is. A villain or a contact for a Great Game in Vienna; talk about boundaries before he sits at your table.

people.name: Gennaro Esposito
people.text: Majordomo to a Neapolitan family, a foundling with the foundlings' surname, who keeps the books, knows the law, hires the crews and decides who knows what. Find him in a back room above a chandler's shop, or at Thursday coffee near the Mercato with the other family's majordomo. He wants to stay the one person the family can't do without, and keeps three ledgers to manage it, one of them true. A patron who hires a party and already knows what it knows.

people.name: Fra Bertrand de Montclar
people.text: A gold-scaled dragonborn knight of the Order of St John, a younger son of the Langue of Provence with sixteen quarterings, holding Candia's breaches in the siege's last year. After dark he's in a casemate on the Sant'Andrea bastion, losing at dice to Venetian sappers on a gaming set a professed knight mustn't touch, and he confesses it on Saturdays. In the breach his sword lights like a church window and the men beside him can't be afraid; he goes in each time because the oath doesn't ask whether the city will hold. An ally or patron for anyone who wants something out of Candia before it falls.

people.name: Ilyanor Sael
people.text: Lanternhall's elf, Attending Physician and Chair of Vital Studies (see Running Euphonia, Notable People). Find him on rounds on the Long Ward at the sixth bell, or in his office above the Library of Cases at any hour; he doesn't leave the Hall. He wants his graduates licensed in the countries they go home to, which makes him a patron for any Physician party and a problem for every licensing office in Europe.

people.name: Sister Ondine
people.text: The senior night sister on Lanternhall's Long Ward, who can't cast a spell and is the one person in the Hall every Physician obeys. Find her on the night watch, or in the corridor outside Ilyanor Sael's office with a teapot; she has threatened him with a blanket, and wants to see him sleep in a bed, once, with his eyes shut. She knows which patients will die by the way they ask for water. An ally, the ward's conscience and its comedy, and the one who sends an exhausted student to bed.

people.name: Anselme Lafrenaye
people.text: The graying halfling Gamester of the French court (see Running Euphonia, Notable People), with his own chair at the end of the lansquenet table at the king's high play, at Saint-Germain most weeks. He knows what Pascal and Fermat wrote to each other about dice, and generals who won't be seen asking a card player the odds lose to him first and ask afterward. He wants to know how he lost a hand he couldn't have lost, to a man who shouldn't have known the odds. A Counsellor's patron, rival or model.

people.name: Kit Harrow
people.text: The Sharper of the Sharper and the Wit (see Running Euphonia, Notable People): a Cavalier baronet's daughter who learned hazard to win back the estate her father lost at the Groom Porter's, and never stopped. Find her at hazard in the Groom Porter's in winter, the card rooms of Tunbridge Wells in August, or Paris when London gets too hot. She wants the estate back or, failing that, to be owed more than anyone in England. A player character as written, an ally or a rival across the table.

people.name: Ned Ashcombe
people.text: The Wit (see Running Euphonia, Notable People): a Royalist colonel's younger son whose lampoons everyone in London can sing. Find him working the room at whatever table Kit Harrow is playing, or at dawn among the king's ducks in St James's Park. He wants the place at court the Restoration promised his father's son, on terms that don't cost him Kit. A player character as written, an ally or a rival; nobody listens to his couplets closely enough to notice they're signals.

people.name: Étaín of the Ford
people.text: A wild elf of the Bordermarches who has ridden with the Wild Hunt since before the parish churches were built. A village meets her at the ford below it on the first dark night after Samhain, hounds ahead of her, her body turned in its skin by the ríastrad; between Beltane and Samhain she hardly thinks of villages at all. She has never been able to throw away a child's wooden horse from a raid three hundred years ago, and wants to know whose it was. A villain for a game on the Border, or a foil someone patient could talk to in the light half.

people.name: Morfudd Prys
people.text: A dwarf of the old mines on the Welsh border, one of the low Hidden who took the shape and forgot, who keeps the gate against the Hidden for her village. Find her at her cottage by the gate, or walking the boundary at dusk on any night of the dark half with a mastiff, an iron bell and her buff coat worn inside out. She wants to find the last Killer, her parent, taken on a Samhain night when she was twelve. An ally or teacher on the Border; the new magistrate thinks she's a cunning woman and would like to see her license.

people.name: Tadhg Ó Laoi
people.text: A Connacht fiddler of Queen Elizabeth's time who played one night under the hill and came home a century late, to the Ireland of the transplantation. Hear him at a wedding or a new landlord's dinner, playing for his supper, or in a shebeen on a fair night where an old woman has started to cry at a tune nobody alive should know. He wants to learn what he owes the Hidden before they come to collect it. An ally and a contact, with a purse of harp shillings no one will take.

regions.intro: The setting's own people here: where a party meets them, what they want and how a table uses them. Simbarashe Moyo, Tonderai Shumba, Tsitsi, Rashid bin Khamis al-Ghafiri, Nyarai Soko and Fadzai Shoko have pregen sheets.

people.name: Simbarashe Moyo
people.text: Mutapa's great artificer, about eighty, who showed that lightning is magic's purest force and lost the fight to keep the art at home (see Running Euphonia, Notable People). Knock at his workshop in Sofala's old town any evening, and the iron construct will already be at the door; he wears a work coat with too many pockets and a burn on the cuff he won't have mended. He wants one honest conversation about the lightning with someone who isn't trying to buy it. A mentor or patron, and the man whose choice a party can force.

people.name: Shiri
people.text: Mutapa's spymaster (see Powers and Factions, The Spymaster), who runs the foreign service from one room above the House of the Bird with a tenth of her rivals' assets. Nobody meets her: a party meets her factor in Sofala or Hoerikwaggo and gets a letter sealed with a soapstone bird, and a very few climb the stairs. She wants one more agent in Europe who can pass at court, and would settle for one who can pass at dinner. A patron who pays on time, every time, which in her trade is a kind of tenderness.

people.name: Tonderai Shumba
people.text: The king's lion at Sofala's outermost gate, a Lionskin Guardian in a lion-helmed suit with a copper-wire mane, under the captain of the gates. Meet him at dawn, when the merchant houses' carters line up to argue the fee: he knows every carter by name, agrees warmly that the road is theirs, and keeps the gate shut. He has been posted to four gates without changing jobs, because the city keeps moving its edge outward, and wants one that stays put a whole season. An ally or a foil, and Sofala's new border in one man.

people.name: Tsitsi
people.text: The go-between at Hoerikwaggo, a Khoekhoe woman of twenty-five raised in the harbor town and the most useful person at the Cape to four powers. Find her on the harbor steps when a ship comes in, translating for everyone at once, every word exact except, now and then, one. The town calls her Tsitsi, Shona for mercy; her own name she keeps to herself, and what she wants is her people's grazing, cattle and terms kept, whatever flag is in the bay. A contact or ally, owned by none of the parties who think they own her.

people.name: Rashid bin Khamis al-Ghafiri
people.text: A Muscat dhow captain with the storm in his blood, an air elemental-blood since lightning climbed down the mast to him as a young deckhand. Find him on any quay from Pate to Kilwa when the northeast monsoon brings the dhows in, selling fair winds by the knot to captains who swear they don't need them; a knot holds until his next sleep. He wants to keep carrying dates and Gulf horses instead of guns for as long as the imam, Sultan bin Saif, lets him, and the imam's officers have started asking about his hold. A patron or rival on the Monsoon Road.

people.name: Ambuya Rudo Gumbo
people.text: The senior royal medium, through whom a king two centuries dead speaks on rain and war, and who has lately said things about the shewstones the living king didn't want to hear. Find her at court on the plateau on the day the royal spirit is asked a question, seated on a mat and already somewhere else, or at home the next day shelling groundnuts, cross about it. She remembers nothing of what he says, returns the shewstone house's gifts unopened, and wants to be spoken to for an afternoon as herself. A patron or ally on the mediums' side of the question of who governs.

people.name: Munyaradzi Shava
people.text: Master of the Shava house, the merchant house that carries the king's shewstones abroad and now stands half a step behind the king's left shoulder. Find him in his counting room in Sofala's new quarter, or at court, listening without blinking and remembering the exact weight of everything you say; it was his men who went to the great artificer's workshop at night. He came back from a lowland fever at twenty-two without whatever makes a man flinch, and wants, once, to be surprised. The Great Game's villain on Mutapa's side, or its best-paying patron.

people.name: Nyarai Soko
people.text: Master of the Mhizha Guild, who swept the great artificer's floor at fourteen and wrote down how he did things so that others could, which he has never quite forgiven. Find her at the guild hall in Sofala on entry day, reading each new journeyman's name aloud twice, with a vial from every batch of the week lined up at her elbow. She wants Simbarashe to come to one entry day and watch the names go onto the rolls. A patron or foil, and the guild's stamp in person.

people.name: Fadzai Shoko
people.text: One of Mutapa's two healers at Hoerikwaggo, a Vitalist who treats the town under the mountain as one patient and the mountain as part of it. Find her at the fever house on the slope with every shutter open at noon, or on the road to a Khoekhoe camp with a basket and an almanac. When the sickness comes there will be more patients than she can reach, and she wants to talk over whom to treat first with someone who doesn't work for anyone. An ally or contact for the ship with the fever (see Hooks).

people.name: Dona Catarina de Sá
people.text: An Afro-Portuguese prazo heiress who lost her land below Tete when Mutapa kept its mines, and now runs the platinum runners of Sofala. Find her at a cook-shop by the fish market at the hottest hour, shelling prawns and asking after your family by name, though she has never met them. Nobody caught with platinum in Sofala can say where it came from, because she makes sure they never knew, and she pays her runners' widows. A villain or contact on the Monsoon Road; a Lisbon lawyer says a European court might honor her deed, and she hasn't decided whether she wants it back.

people.name: Mwalimu Bakari Shee
people.text: A Bajuni pilot of Faza, a water elemental-blood who went over the side in a squall at fourteen and came up three days later a mile out, breathing easily, with a promise to someone in the deep that he still keeps. Find him sitting on an upturned hull on the beach at Faza or the Lamu waterfront when a captain needs a pilot for deep water. He knows which waters take a toll, leaves a gift over certain soundings without explaining, and wants one passage on which nothing below asks him for anything. An ally or contact, and a Dreamlord Warlock of the deep in person.

regions.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn
regions.intro: The setting's own people here: where a party meets them, what they want and how a table uses them. Mustafa Remzi Efendi, Yusuf Rais, Wäldä Mika'el, Farrokh of Isfahan, Golnar and Nafisa al-Qalyubiyya have pregen sheets.

people.name: Mustafa Remzi Efendi
people.text: The *müneccimbaşı*, the Ottoman chief astrologer and so the empire's minister of magic: an astronomer in Taqi al-Din's line who picks the hour by measurement. Find him on a terrace of the Topkapı an hour before dawn, astrolabe at arm's length, while the court waits in the cold for his finger to lift. The Kadızadeli preachers want him gone and the Köprülü viziers need him; he wants to be left alone with his instruments long enough to finish tables the Frankish astronomers will have to copy. A patron or mentor, with a Mutapan device in parts on his table.

people.name: Yusuf Rais
people.text: A captain of the *taifa*, Algiers' corsair captains' guild, born Tom Penhale of Falmouth. Meet him at the stern of his galley when a ransom boat comes out under a flag of truce, or at the taifa's counting house by the mole, pricing every name on a ransom list in three currencies without looking up. He takes ships, ransoms what he takes and buys Muslim captives back out of Malta and Livorno, and wants both sets of books balanced, the guild's and his own, with nobody reading the second. A patron or rival for any ransom job (see Hooks).

people.name: Wäldä Mika'el
people.text: A *däbtära* of Gondar, an unordained church scholar, cantor and poet who writes God's secret names on healing scrolls for Christian, Muslim and Beta Israel clients alike. Find him in a courtyard where a child is sick, with a scroll he finished at dawn, or over coffee arguing unction with the monks from Gojjam; this year's council has made his client list a complicated document. He wants to go to Enfraz and argue with Zera Yacob, the old scholar there who tests every religion by reason. An ally or teacher, and a good friend to have when a *buda* charge is made.

people.name: Farrokh of Isfahan
people.text: The pari-touched elf (see The Hidden Here), who went to a pari wedding at Nowruz, ate at the feast and came back three years later in the wedding robe, green silk gone sea-gray at the hems. Find him in the corner of a coffeehouse off the Maidan after the evening prayer, letting a water pipe bubble that he doesn't inhale. He wants the way back in and can't leave it alone. He can tell by looking who else has been to the wedding and come back, so the families of the taken find him: an ally or contact for the pari wedding (see Hooks).

people.name: Khadijeh Khatun
people.text: Stewardess of the shah's mother's household, called the Key, who decides which letters, petitions and rumors go in to the women who decide what reaches the shah. Meet her in a garden pavilion of the royal harem, through a screen, with sherbet already poured for the number of visitors she was told to expect. She has someone in every great house in Isfahan, usually a cook, and wants her nephew placed in the chancery and her own name kept out of every European's travel book. A patron or rival for a Great Game at Isfahan.

people.name: Khodadad the Dyer
people.text: The Zoroastrian dyer who was set on the throne before the second coronation to take the bad stars off the shah (see Magic Here); it worked, and as far as anyone can tell he still has them. Find him knee-deep in a dye vat in Isfahan's Zoroastrian quarter, arms blue to the elbow, hoping you're a customer; when he hears who sent you, he sits down in the dye. He wants to be forgotten, or failing that, for his daughter's wedding to go ahead with nothing going wrong at it. The heart of the substitute (see Hooks): one court faction wants him safe and quiet, another wants him back on the throne for an afternoon.

people.name: Shushan Ghukasian
people.text: The widowed head of a New Julfa silk house with partners in Surat, Venice and Amsterdam, who hires crews for the Bandar Abbas and Surat run and pays in credit good from Amsterdam to Manila. Find her in her counting room off the Vank cathedral square, reading a bill of exchange, a manifest and your faces in that order. Her younger son went to a pari wedding at Nowruz with a flute and hasn't come back; she has paid a priest, a dervish and an astrologer, and decided it's time for people who carry swords. The patron of the pari wedding (see Hooks), and a Monsoon Road employer after.

people.name: Golnar
people.text: A pari of the bride's family at the wedding Farrokh ran from, holding a shape in Isfahan to get the painted glass cup back, and remembering every minute of what she is. Find her by a fountain on the Maidan at dusk, in a green nobody else seems to notice; when she sits at your table, every water flask you carry is suddenly full of rosewater. She wants the cup back unbroken and Farrokh returned to the feast of his own free will, which she thinks kinder than the other way, and she knows where Shushan Ghukasian's son is and won't say. A villain or foil, polite, patient and bound by every promise she makes.

people.name: Hafız Ömer
people.text: A young Kadızadeli preacher in Istanbul, honest, learned and certain that the lodges, the coffee and the talisman-makers are innovations the Prophet never knew. Find him in a neighborhood pulpit at Friday prayer, or at the gate of a shuttered Sufi lodge with fifty listeners behind him. His prayers work, which he takes as proof he's right; he would close the lodges and carry a dervish's shopping home on the way, and his followers don't always wait for the court. A foil or rival, who wants his mother to take off her charm against the evil eye and listen to him once.

people.name: Nafisa al-Qalyubiyya
people.text: A physician of al-Mansuri, the Cairo hospital that has taught at the bedside for nearly four hundred years, who runs its plague service and finds Lanternhall's fame puzzling. Find her on the wards, or in a plague lane at Bulaq with a censer, a veil and a ledger. She noticed in 1651 what Lanternhall noticed, that a patient cured by magic catches the same fever again, and wants her notes read by someone in Basel who will take them seriously. A mentor or contact for any Physician.

people.name: Nane Gulbahar
people.text: A Tabriz midwife who keeps the forty days after a birth against the Āl, and has never lost a mother to her. Find her on a stool across a new mother's doorway through the night, an iron sickle on her knees and onions and garlic over the lintel; when something thin with a clay nose looks round the gate, she says its name without getting up. She says the trick isn't courage but staying awake, and wants an apprentice with younger knees who isn't afraid of the dark. A mentor or ally, and a Hidden Killer by another name.

regions.intro: The setting's own people here: where a party meets them, what they want and how a table uses them. Akinwale, Dom Garcia Nsaku and Buatu Makaya have pregen sheets.

people.name: Akinwale
people.text: A front-rank horseman of Oyo's cavalry who is ridden by his orisha in battle and remembers none of it. Find him in the horse lines outside Oyo Ile in the dry season, rubbing down a Nupe war-horse that cost more than his house and arguing with its fodder; he looks at your horse's eyes before he looks at yours. He wants that horse alive through one more rainy season, and to hear from someone who saw it what he was laughing at in the ford. An ally or contact, and the man to ask about the master of horse's job (see Hooks).

people.name: Dom Garcia Nsaku
people.text: A Soyo shield-bearer who carries Count Paulo da Silva's letters to people who would rather not receive them, and comes back. Find him in the plaza at Mbanza Soyo after Mass, teaching boys the sword in the church's shade, or at your door with a sealed letter he has never read. He hears Mass from the Capuchins and stops at the nganga's door on the way home to ask after the count's oath-bundle, and sees no contradiction; he wants to learn whether Soyo means to reunite Kongo, rule it or keep it broken before he is asked to fight for the answer. An ally or patron, and Soyo's man on the road if Count Paulo sends to Sofala.

people.name: Olaniyi
people.text: Master of the Alaafin's horse, sworn into the Ogboni, who knows to the animal how many mounts Oyo has, how many it can buy from Nupe and how many the forest will kill. Find him in the royal stables at Oyo Ile before the dry-season campaign, a tally-stick in each hand and a groom at each elbow. He wants one person who can keep a horse alive past the tsetse line and would forgive them almost anything; several people would rather that person didn't exist. The patron of the horse (see Hooks).

people.name: Ayoka
people.text: A chanter of *oríkì*, the praise poetry of Oyo's families, who knows every lineage's glories and the parts it leaves out. Find her in Akinwale's quarter on a festival day, chanting each family as it passes, louder for the ones who tip; she'll greet you with a line of praise for your grandfather, made up on the spot and better than anything he did. She has added a line about laughing to Akinwale's oríkì, and wants a line in her own worth chanting. A contact who trades what she knows for a story she hasn't heard.

people.name: Buatu Makaya
people.text: A Vili merchant of Loango who carries copper and cloth to Malebo Pool and speaks the language of every valley on the road, including some no one taught him. Find him at the Tio markets in the dry season, unloading his porters, already on his third language of the morning. He climbed the hill behind his village on a dare at twelve and came down a week later speaking Teke, and he wants to find the valley whose language he has dreamed in ever since. A contact, and the best guide on the copper road for a party that wants to arrive with its manners intact.

people.name: Ndona Nsimba
people.text: A nganga of Soyo who heals, divines, guards against the ndoki and makes the oath minkisi that seal the count's treaties. Find her at her compound on the edge of the sacred wood of Nfinda Ngula at dusk, binding an oath bundle in cloth and cord, or haggling with a Dutch trader over a fever cure. She and the Capuchin heal the same fevers in the same streets under an arrangement neither admits to, and she wants him to stop burning her work and start asking what it's for. An ally or teacher; lords who break an oath sworn on one of her bundles have been known to sicken.

people.name: Dona Isabel Mvemba
people.text: A Kongo noblewoman widowed at Mbwila, who swore over her husband's body to bring the king's crown and scepter home from Lisbon, and the oath took. Find her in a borrowed house in Mbanza Soyo, in her late husband's best cloak, receiving visitors as if the kingdom were still whole, a Portuguese grammar and a list of Lisbon-bound ships on the table. She needs a crew that can pass in Lisbon, and is honest that what her house does with the crown afterward is her house's business. The patron of the crown in Lisbon (see Hooks).

people.name: Osaretin
people.text: A master of the oba's guild of brass-casters in Benin City, who casts the court's history in metal and can read a room's ranks from where people stand. Watch him from the doorway of the casters' street in the heat of a pour, and not one step further. He has heard that Europe's ministers of magic are reading about Benin's palace in Dapper's new book, and wants to see it with his own eyes and find out what the Dutch got wrong. A contact at the oba's court, and a reason to carry a book from Amsterdam.

people.name: Akosua Nyarko
people.text: An Akan hunter who walks the forest's edge behind Accra for her village, keeps the owners' rules and deals with what doesn't. Find her in the harmattan at the shrine where the path enters the trees, crouched over a line of backward footprints a foot long, laughing quietly. She has met the mmoatia three times and wants to learn what they teach the priests without paying the priests' price. An ally or guide for a game on the Border, for a fair fee and the promise that you'll do exactly as she says at the shrines.

people.name: Alfa Mahmud Gurdu
people.text: Keeper of a Timbuktu family library near the Sankore mosque that outlasted the Moroccan conquest and the Arma, and a master of the science of letters. Find him in the cool before noon, lying on a mat with a manuscript propped on his chest, correcting a student's grammar without opening his eyes. His grandfather walled up a room when the Moroccans carried the scholars away, the family is still unwalling it shelf by shelf, and he wants a copyist with a steady hand and a good memory. A mentor or patron who pays in knowledge, which he considers the more generous currency.

people.name: Sossi
people.text: A market woman of Allada who has sold everything she can sell and walked to the beach at Offra to buy her brother back before the company ship sails. Find her beside a company lodge, counting cowries on a mat in her best cloth and never once looking at the ship. The factor's price went up when he saw she could pay it, and she needs someone who can talk to the captain, the king's man who sold her brother, or anyone. The patron of the roads at Offra (see Hooks), who will owe a party for the rest of her life and pay it.

regions.intro: The setting's own people here: where a party meets them, what they want and how a table uses them. Kesavan Vaidyan, Amritnath and Rakhmabai Deshmukh have pregen sheets.

people.name: Kesavan Vaidyan
people.text: A Malabar surgeon whose family craft is the nose rebuilt from the patient's own skin, and whose knife floats while his hands stay folded in his lap. Find him on his veranda in the monsoon months, when the roads are mud and the patients come anyway, from both sides of the nose-cutting wars between Mysore and Madurai, passing each other on his road without speaking. He charges the poor in rice and the poligars in gold and gives both the same attention, and he wants to see a nose he rebuilt twenty years ago and know that it held. A mentor or ally for any Physician.

people.name: Amritnath
people.text: A Nath yogi who has stopped aging and no longer needs food, water or air, and takes all three out of courtesy. Find him at dawn at his *dhuni* on the pilgrim road above the Ganges plain, with a raja's men already waiting to ask how to live forever; he lets them wait until noon. He gives the old inoculation against smallpox to anyone who sits still, finds the hospital in Basel charming and wants the last *siddhi*, the deathless body. A mentor, or a foil to Lanternhall's Ilyanor Sael, who stopped reaching for the same thing.

people.name: Manekbai Parekh
people.text: A Jain shroff's widow who runs her late husband's banking house in Surat and writes hundis honored from Mocha to Malacca. Find her in the cool upper room near the customs house in the weeks before the ships sail, doing sums aloud in Gujarati faster than the English president's writer can do them on paper. She'll stake a party's voyage at a rate that depends on how much she likes them, and she likes very few; she wants her grandson to take the house before her husband's brothers do. A Monsoon Road patron, who reminds the House of the Bird's factor where it learned credit.

people.name: Kunhi Ayesha
people.text: A Mappila pepper broker on the Calicut beach who sells the Zamorin's officers news of every ship, and every ship news of the Zamorin's officers. Find her under a palm-leaf awning at the pepper weighing, sorting peppercorns without looking while repeating word for word what a Dutch captain said three tables away. She wants her son's ship back from Mocha before the southwest monsoon closes the coast. A contact or ally; she sends Kesavan Vaidyan the patients who come in on ships.

people.name: Abdul Wahid
people.text: The Surat muhtasib's clerk, who reads every foreigner's permit to practice magic and checks whether the official who signed it is still in office. Find him behind the customs house, holding a Company wizard's permit up to the window and asking after the signing official's health. He is honest, pious, underpaid and very good at his job, and wants to be the first clerk in Surat to read the emperor's new law book and find that it agrees with him. A foil for a permit nobody will name (see Hooks), and the worst man a smuggler can meet.

people.name: Rakhmabai Deshmukh
people.text: A Maratha deshmukh's widow who took the fort's keys from her husband's belt before the funeral and holds his hill fort in the Western Ghats for Shivaji. Find her on the gate bastion at dusk, counting the Mughal patrol fires on the plain, or at a truce table, winning. The peace with the viceroy is holding, she is using it to repair walls, and she wants it to last until her daughter's wedding. A patron or rival, who plays chess with the enemy and wins in the margins.

people.name: Kunwar Ratan Singh
people.text: A younger prince of a minor Hada Rajput house, serving in the Mughal army of the Deccan, who fences like water and has never lost his temper in public. Find him on the practice ground of the viceroy's camp at Aurangabad at first light, or wherever a Maratha envoy is being entertained. Rakhmabai Deshmukh has beaten him at chess twice across a truce table and he would like a third game; what he wants most is a deed to land of his own rather than his elder brother's. A rival, a love interest or a gracious enemy.

people.name: Ammakka
people.text: A dwarf diamond appraiser of Golconda, of a family that says it came from the treasure-keeping yakshas, who has started testing whether a diamond can do for magic what platinum does for Mutapa. Find her at the grading in Kollur at dawn, a rough stone in tongs in a lamp flame, timing something by her pulse. Her trials so far are inconclusive and twice explosive, the notebook lives in a pot of rice, and she wants a clean answer with nobody from three crowns watching. A contact or patron for the untested stone (see Hooks).

people.name: Ponni
people.text: A potter-priest's daughter of seventeen in a village near Madurai, who helps make Ayyanar's terracotta horses and has started riding out behind them at the boundary. Find her at the Ayyanar shrine among the clay horses on a dark-half night, walking the boundary with a sickle and a clay lamp. She has better hands for clay than either brother and a better seat on a horse that isn't there, and wants her father to let her make one horse that is hers alone. An ally, quietly furious about almost everything, and a Hidden Killer just starting out.

people.name: Saadat Ali
people.text: An Agra bridegroom who went to a pari wedding, came back after what he swears was one night, and found it had been three years and he was married twice. Find him on a doorstep near the Jamuna at midnight, outside his bride's family's house, playing a rabab tune he never learned while every dog in the lane lies down to listen. He wants his human bride's forgiveness, and hasn't told her he'd go back. Comic relief, a love interest and the groom of a pari wedding (see Hooks).

regions.intro: The setting's own people here: where a party meets them, what they want and how a table uses them. Lu Qingxu, Shi Yuanjing, Tachibana Chiyo, Daeng Calla, Hu Lanxin and Brother Joris Vanhove have pregen sheets.

people.name: Lu Qingxu
people.text: The last of a line of Ming court alchemists, one of the Qiu Xian Zhe (see Powers and Factions, Seekers of Immortality), in Daoist dress that keeps the queue off his head and the questions off his past. Find him at a hill hermitage with a luopan on the table and the Bureau's old sealing calendar open beside it, or at the last door of a tomb by lamplight. He carries a red pill from the batch his teacher died of, and wants to learn whether the batch was wrong, or the teacher. An ally or mentor who digs where the sealing dates don't add up: the Tomb Road's fallen alchemist, ready to go.

people.name: Shi Yuanjing
people.text: A Shaolin fighting monk the abbot sends down alone with a staff to meet whatever official comes up the valley road, because he is calm, polite and plainly impossible to arrest. Find him at the monastery gate on Mount Song, or sitting on the gate tower's lintel, which he reached by walking three steps up its face. Given to the monastery in a famine year, he is still grateful for the millet; his ordination certificate dates from the last Ming years, and no Qing clerk has asked to see it yet. He wants not to have to decide what he'll do when the governor tells the monks to stop drilling; until then, an ally or teacher.

people.name: Tachibana Chiyo
people.text: An aasimar shrine priestess in a mountain province of Japan, born with the light in her, who is sent for when a child is lost at dusk (see The Hidden Here). Find her at the shrine at dusk, sandals by the lantern, when someone comes running. She has never seen a foreigner and doesn't expect to, and wants, once, to walk the road to the pass and back without being needed. An ally for a child hidden by the kami, or by something that isn't one.

people.name: Daeng Calla
people.text: A Makassarese halfling smuggler with a share in a padewakang, who moves Mutapan curiosities without a ministry stamp and carries letters out through the lines at Somba Opu. Find her in the hold off Makassar after dark with her own lamp switched off, or smiling at a Dutch boarding officer and telling him the long crate is rattan. Her lamps drift every month, and she wants someone with Mutapan training aboard. An ally or contact for the last sortie (see Hooks); her grandmother says the family came from the orang bunian, and she says that explains the hiding and nothing else.

people.name: Gu Wenyuan
people.text: A dragonborn calendar clerk of Yang Guangxian's Astronomical Bureau, who will be out of work the day the shadow falls the Jesuits' way and has found a Ming prince's sealing date that doesn't add up. Find him at the observatory on the city wall at night, or in a teahouse nearby doing long division on a tea bill with his sleeve pulled down over the scales on his wrist. He wants to prove the arithmetic wrong before anyone burns the records, mostly so someone will know he was right. The clerk (see Hooks) who opens the Tomb Road: a patron or a fellow delver.

people.name: Shen Xuanji
people.text: A fallen court alchemist, seventy-four and looking forty-five, who compounds mineral elixirs for rich men in Beijing. Find him by introduction only, after dark, in the back room of a medicine shop near the Drum Tower that smells of mercury. His illusions are first-rate and his elixirs are mercury; he has decided Lu Qingxu's teacher found something real, and he wants to be young, actually. The Tomb Road's villain, always one tomb ahead.

people.name: Hu Lanxin
people.text: A fox spirit in a woman's shape who remembers what she is, and wants the party's tomb for the fox-jade buried with a prince who once loved her. Meet her already inside a sealed Ming tomb when the party breaks through, sitting on the coffin eating their dried plums and asking what took them so long. She is honest about everything except her age, wants the jade back because it's hers, and wants to know whether he was buried holding it. A rival or love interest on the Tomb Road.

people.name: Brother Joris Vanhove
people.text: A Flemish Jesuit lay brother in Beijing who can cast a cannon, mend a clock and compute a noon shadow, and is checking every figure he can before December. Find him in the workshop behind the Jesuit chapel, or kneeling in the courtyard with a plumb line, waiting for noon and refusing to be spoken to. He likes the Bureau's Chinese astronomers better than the Portuguese fathers, thinks the gnomon trial the most honest test he'll ever see, and is terrified. A contact or ally for the witness (see Hooks).

people.name: Ok Rye-hwa
people.text: A Korean *mudang* outside Seoul's walls, who bargains with the spirits for her neighbors, pays the state's tax on shamans and is despised by the scholars who send for her at night. Find her at a *gut* with the drums going since dusk, dancing barefoot on the blades of two fodder-choppers in a general's hat. She has argued with the spirits on behalf of a castaway Dutch sailor, a magistrate's widow and a drowned ox, and wants her daughter to inherit the drum and the clients without the contempt. An ally or contact for any game in Joseon.

people.name: Teungku Fatimah
people.text: A scholar of the science of letters at the court of Aceh's queen, Sultanah Safiatuddin, who writes the talismans on the port's walls and is one reason the Dutch knock before entering. Find her in the hall where scholars read before the queen, or on the quay when a ship from Surat comes in with books. She wants a book of letters she has only seen quoted, said to be in a Bohra library in Surat, and pays for books in pepper, generously. A Monsoon Road patron.

people.name: Chea Sok
people.text: A Khmer former monk called by spirit illness at Angkor, who sees the temple as the world-mountain it was built to be and guides pilgrims through it by night. Find him keeping vigil with a clay lamp in the gallery of the Thousand Buddhas at Angkor Wat, describing with complete calm the five peaks above the central tower that nobody else can see. He left the monastery with his abbot's blessing, and wants to know why the mountain answered a Japanese pilgrim who thought he was somewhere else. A mentor or contact for any game at Angkor (see Angkor).

regions.intro: The setting's own people here: where a party meets them, what they want and how a table uses them. Waman Illa, Čhaŋté Wašté Wiŋ, Willka Mamani and Doña Isabel Cuauhtzin have pregen sheets.

people.name: Waman Illa
people.text: A storm-priest of the high valleys above the Apurímac, struck by lightning as a boy herder, who keeps a huaca that rose in the Taki Onqoy years and speaks for it to the Sapa Inca's officers, and for them to it. Officers climb to his shelf above the Apurímac crossing with khipus of the Spanish column and leave with rain, and a list of what the huaca wants in return; he offers everyone coca while they decide whether to pay. He wants to see the war end before the huaca decides it likes it. A patron or ally for an Inca start in The High Ground (see Adventures and Hooks).

people.name: Čhaŋté Wašté Wiŋ
people.text: A Dakota druid of the lake country around Mille Lacs who hunts bison on foot with her people and takes the bison's shape, a fact about her rather than a secret. Meet her at the prairie edge during the fall hunt, or in the camps on the lakes when the wild rice is ripe, letting the young men tell her story wrong. She wants a good harvest, a quiet winter and no black-robed visitors; she has seen one Frenchman, at a distance, carrying a kettle, and has not felt the lack. An ally or mentor on her own ground, where she has enough to do.

people.name: Kusi Wallpa
people.text: The Sapa Inca's senior staff officer on the Apurímac front, who reads Spanish columns by their dust and empties the storehouses on their road before they arrive. Find him on a cold rock above a column's road, a khipu across his knees and a runner waiting. He hires outsiders for what a khipu can't do (reading a Spanish captain, buying a mule-driver, finding who in Potosí sells powder to both sides) and pays in cloth, safe roads and his word. The patron of an Inca start in The High Ground, who wants one season in which nobody he counts into a khipu has to be counted out.

people.name: Willka Mamani
people.text: A Kallawaya healer of Charazani who walks the war's roads with close to a thousand plants in his head, treating Inca runners and Spanish muleteers alike. Find him on the road between the lines with a mule and a woven bag of medicines, stopping wherever someone is sick. Both armies let him through because both need him, and he sells each exactly as much news of the other; he wants an apprentice who can remember the plants and keep quiet. An ally, a mentor and the best guide across the line alive.

people.name: Licenciado Diego Ruiz de Lezcano
people.text: A visitor-general of idolatries for the Archbishop of Lima, who burns the mummified dead and the stones that speak, and whose prayers work, which he takes as proof. Find him at a table in a highland plaza with a notary, soldiers and a bonfire laid but not yet lit, calling the village's ancestors by name in a gentle voice and writing down who doesn't answer. He is sincere, learned and kind to children, and wants one village where the stone stays silent after he has prayed over it. A villain for the visitations (see Trouble Brewing), and a frightened man.

people.name: Aj K'in Kuch
people.text: An Itza priest who reads the k'atun count for the Aj Kan Ek' at Nojpetén, and has seen, past the edge of the world, why it is not yet time. Find him on temple steps at dawn with a screenfold book across his knees, telling a friar politely and precisely that he has come twenty-nine years too early. He wants to train someone to read the count after him before the Spanish road reaches the lake, and wants the surveyor never to arrive. A patron or mentor for the survey (see Hooks).

people.name: Ganonhsese
people.text: An Onondaga Clan Mother, among the Firekeepers of the Haudenosaunee, who chooses her clan's chief for the Grand Council and can remove him. Find her in her longhouse at Onondaga in winter, when the stories may be told, shelling beans with her daughters while a council chief explains himself to her. Somebody has neglected the Jogah and the drumming has started with no drummer; she wants it put right so the winter's stories can be told, and her grandson home from the western war. The patron of the drumming (see Hooks), who pays in the Confederacy's remembering.

people.name: Kima Ismare
people.text: A Wounaan *jaibaná* of the upper San Juan, hired by her people to keep a river shut against the mining families from Popayán, who have hired another jaibaná to open it. Find her cross-legged under her stilt house where the miners' canoes stop and turn back, talking to something in the river that isn't the river. She has kept it shut six years, and wants to outlast her rival, a man she trained and is not proud of. A patron or foil for opening the river (see Hooks), paid in fish, cloth and the right to be cross with everyone.

people.name: Ana Kitumba
people.text: A captain of Palmares, born free behind the palisade at Macaco after her mother came up from a Pernambuco sugar mill with a baby and nothing else. Find her walking the palisade at dusk with a spear and a Portuguese musket, greeting every sentry by name, or at council in the king's house. Her oath is to the people who got free and to the ones still coming, and it has never once failed her; she wants a child of hers to grow old in Palmares without having to fight for it. An ally or patron.

people.name: Brás Furtado
people.text: A *capitão-do-mato*, a hunter of people who escaped slavery, whom the sugar planters of Pernambuco hire to lead their expeditions against Palmares. Find him at a planters' dinner in Porto Calvo where a new expedition is being priced, naming the price per head without looking up. He has studied every expedition that failed against Palmares and knows why each did, which is why Ana Kitumba knows his name. A villain from a hard part of the record; a table chooses how much of him to use.

people.name: Doña Isabel Cuauhtzin
people.text: A Nahua cacica of a noble Xochimilco family who paints portrait miniatures for the viceroy's court in Mexico City, and so holds the likeness of everyone worth scrying in New Spain. Find her at a palace window with a vellum oval no bigger than her palm, catching a marquis's exact expression while he thinks she's painting his sleeve. She keeps her family's records in Nahuatl and its lawsuit over their Xochimilco lands in Spanish, and has started, very quietly, painting her likenesses slightly wrong. A contact for a Great Game in New Spain; three services want her sketchbooks.

regions.intro: The setting's own people here: where a party meets them, what they want and how a table uses them. Sehpin, Kilimoar and Kaiawa have pregen sheets.

people.name: Sehpin
people.text: A yam-grower's child the basalt answered at fifteen, now one of the few left who can raise a course at Nan Madol, and the keeper of the people behind the walls. Find them waist-deep in the shallows at dusk with a palm on a fallen column, or at the feast house the day the prize yams come in. A Nahnmwarki asks for their work and so do the samworo, and neither has it by right; Sehpin wants to stop being asked to choose. A patron or mentor: when traders off the Monsoon Road ask how the stones were raised, Sehpin tells them the truth, that you ask, and they write it down as if it were a lie (see Hooks).

people.name: Kilimoar
people.text: A *samworo*, a priest of Pohnpei, who made Sehpin listen to the basalt for a year before letting them touch it. Find him among the old teachers' stones at Salapwuk, or at Nan Madol at night, laying offerings on a *pei* the chiefs have forgotten. He wants the rites kept by someone after him, and not sold, and would rather Sehpin kept them than built sea walls for a chief. A mentor or rival; when a Monsoon Road trader asked to buy the method, he laughed so long the trader left.

people.name: Lihpahnu
people.text: Sehpin's elder sister, who grows the family's prize yams for the chiefs' feasts and considers this the family's real work. Find her up to her elbows in red earth above the lagoon, or at the feast house the night the yams come in on poles. She loves Sehpin, finds the stones a little showy and wants to grow a yam so large the Nahnmwarki remembers her name and not her sibling's. Anyone who wants Sehpin goes through her kitchen, and she feeds them first and asks questions after.

people.name: Tinashe Gumbo
people.text: A Mutapan Mhizha who came out along the Monsoon Road to learn how Pohnpei's stones were raised, and whether the method can be bought. Find him at the edge of a Nahnmwarki's feast house waiting for leave to see Nan Madol at night, his construct holding a sunshade over him while he asks every passing child the Pohnpeian word for something. He has watched Sehpin talk a column into a wall and is no longer sure what he came to buy. A rival or contact, and the trader of the stones (see Hooks).

people.name: Sarongelug
people.text: A *palu*, a master navigator of the Carolinian wayfinding schools on Polowat, who holds the star compass and the swells in his head. Find him on the beach beside a voyaging canoe, or in a canoe house on Pohnpei waiting out the wrong wind. A Dutch captain offered him a year's silver for a passage no chart shows, and he told the captain, kindly, that the school doesn't sell and the captain couldn't pay. A mentor or contact for a navigator for hire (see Hooks), who wants one more voyage to Guam before the Spanish change it.

people.name: Asiga
people.text: A Chamorro *makåhna* in Hagåtña, a healer and speaker to the ancestors, who will watch San Vitores's mission come ashore in June and must decide what it means for her family. Find her at the edge of the crowd on the beach with a basket of medicines, studying the black-robed men the way she'd study a new plant. Chief Kepuha has welcomed the Jesuits and she respects Kepuha; she hasn't decided whether to be the priests' best friend or their worst problem. A contact or foil for the mission (see Trouble Brewing), who wants her curious daughter not to decide anything quickly.

people.name: Tetua
people.text: A young ʻarioi of ʻOro's society from Raʻiātea, whose troupe mocks the chiefs in dance and verse and is fed handsomely for it. Find her on a chief's performance ground in Tahiti, imitating the chief's walk so exactly that his own sons can't breathe. She has been asked to leave one island and begged to stay on another, and wants to be the one who makes the Tuʻi Tonga's envoy laugh at himself. Comic relief, and a contact who hears what chiefs say when they think the performers are only performing.

people.name: Kaiawa
people.text: A tohunga of a Waikato hapū who heals with the waters that run toward Hawaiki and keeps the pā's fires lit when patupaiarehe flutes sound on the ridge. Find her at a pā above the Waikato River when the mist is down, feeding a cooking fire with red ochre on her hands and listening hard to the ridge. She wants to get through one misty season without a woman of her pā walking toward the flutes, and tells anyone who'll listen that a pause is not a peace. A mentor or ally for the flute (see Hooks).

people.name: Fusipala
people.text: A woman of a chiefly house at Lapaha on Tongatapu who keeps the order of the *ʻinasi*, the first-fruits presentation to the Tuʻi Tonga: whose yams, mats and kava go where, from which island, and what it means when a chief sends less. Find her on a fine mat at the edge of the green in the weeks before, a knotted cord in her lap, telling a young chief gently which of his uncles he has just insulted. The Tuʻi Tonga is sacred and doesn't count things, so she counts them for him, and wants one ʻinasi with no short count sent on purpose. A patron who hires strangers when a canoe goes missing on the way, because a stranger can ask what a chief can't.

people.name: Hoʻolulu
people.text: A *kahuna lāʻau lapaʻau* of Kona on Hawaiʻi Island, a healer by plants and prayer who studied twenty years before he was let near a patient. Find him in the uplands at dawn gathering plants with a prayer for each, or kneeling by a fever with a gourd of pounded leaves, not hurrying for anyone. He has treated the warriors of three rival chiefs and been thanked by all three, and wants an apprentice patient enough to learn a plant's prayer before its use. A mentor or ally; when no plant answers, he goes up the mountain and asks why.

regions.intro: The setting's own people here: where a party meets them, what they want and how a table uses them. Nurbibi has a pregen sheet.

people.name: Nurbibi
people.text: A steppe gnome, the first to study the griffins' kin as animals rather than legends. Find her in a felt blind on a ridge of red sandstone on the ninth day, and don't disturb her; she has watched one brood its eggs on warm quartz and written "a mother" in a careful hand, with the date. Buyers in Bukhara, Moscow and London court her notebooks, and she wants the little monsters described properly, by someone who watched them, before a cabinet gives them a Latin name and the wrong diet. A contact or ally, and the naturalist of the specimen hook, if the table likes.

people.name: Aisulu
people.text: A Kazakh *batyr* of giant blood, a goliath who rides watch for her camp against Dzungar raiders and the Wild Hunt alike. Find her on a ridge of the autumn pasture at dusk, standing in her stirrups a head taller than any rider on the line, a golden eagle on her arm. On the steppe the camp's own riders ride out against the Hunt and she rides first; she hasn't told the camp that the Hunt's best rider has her brother's laugh. An ally who wants her brother Kenzhe home and himself again, and knows the second is harder.

people.name: Kenzhe
people.text: Aisulu's brother, a Kazakh rider taken by the pari three winters ago, who came back riding ahead of the Wild Hunt and takes people rather than killing them. Find him just past a camp's watch fires in the dark half, smiling his old smile and calling the watch by their childhood names. He isn't cruel: he takes people the way you'd carry a friend out of a burning yurt, and he wants to bring his sister across because he truly believes she'd be happier there. A villain or foil; the camp still sets a bowl for him at feasts, and something empties it.

people.name: Zhamal-apa
people.text: A Kazakh midwife of the same camp, a Hedge Witch who drives the albasty off birthing mothers by announcing that a hero has arrived, and pays for every life in her own pain. Find her in a yurt at night with a whip by the threshold and every knot in the tent untied, shouting "The hero has come!" so convincingly that the hero, Aisulu, ducks in looking embarrassed. The lamas call it superstition; she says the lamas have never had a baby. A mentor or ally who wants a girl to train who won't flinch, and not to be sent for in winter.

people.name: Bibi Oysha
people.text: A Bukharan *otin*, a woman teacher, who writes the protective talismans for her father's Naqshbandi lodge and teaches the science of letters to girls the madrasas won't take. Find her in the lodge courtyard drawing a square of letters on a doorframe in saffron ink, a whole courtyard of girls reciting it back. She has outlived half the scholars who said a woman couldn't do it, and wants one of her girls admitted to read in a madrasa library, once, with the door open. A mentor or patron, and the reason the lodge's shelter holds.

people.name: Lala Sukhdev
people.text: A Multani moneylender, one of some five hundred Indian bankers in Bukhara's caravanserais, who lends to herders, khans and madrasa students. Find him on a carpet in an upper room of the Indian caravanserai with his ledgers and a pot of tea, counting a herder's loan onto a cloth twice so the herder can follow. He'll advance a party anything against a bill on Surat, and the Bukhara buyer who wants Nurbibi's live beast writes his offers through him. A patron or contact who wants to go home to Multan for his daughter's wedding without losing his clients to his cousin.

people.name: Tseren Dorji
people.text: A *zaisang*, a Dzungar noble official, who has watched Sengge's half-brothers count their men and wants Sengge's brother home from Tibet before they move. Find him in the khan's tent in the Ili valley, hand never far from his saber, counting the men by the door during a half-brother's toast. He needs someone to carry a letter, and an argument, to teachers in Tibet who can't be ordered, and pays in good Dzungar guns. The patron of the vow (see Hooks), who wants the monk home and the khan alive, in that order if it can't be both.

people.name: Gelong Tsereng
people.text: A Khalkha Buddhist monk of Erdene Zuu who heals the sick on the herding round and burns the shamans' *ongon*, because he honestly believes they hold spirits that harm children. Find him by the courtyard brazier, setting a felt ongon on the coals with real regret, then bandaging the hand of the woman who made it. He enforces the law gently and without exception, and keeps one ongon he couldn't bring himself to burn in a box under his bed. A foil or ally who wants to be thanked by a shaman, once, for a healing.

people.name: Iliqa
people.text: An Evenki shaman of the upper Lena, chosen by a dead shaman's spirit through an illness that lasted three winters, who walks the Tree's three worlds for her clan. Find her drumming in a dark tent at the winter camp until the drum's rim frosts over, or at the Yakutsk fort's gate on tribute day, asking to see the hostage house, where her nephew is held. The fort wants fur, not licenses, and she gives it exactly as many sables as the forest can spare, which is never enough. An ally or mentor for the hostage (see Hooks).

people.name: Avdotya Shchukina
people.text: A Cossack widow who runs a sable-smuggling family from the back room of her late husband's tavern below the Tobolsk kremlin. Find her pouring kvass for a governor's clerk with one hand and sliding a sable pelt to him under the table with her foot. She knows which forts hold hostages for furs that will never come, buys the furs anyway from both sides, and lights a candle for every runner she has lost. A villain or contact who wants her youngest son ordained a priest, a long way from Tobolsk and from her.

people.name: Avetik of Julfa
people.text: A New Julfa merchant's younger son sent to Astrakhan to learn the silk trade, who learned nard instead and wins more from Kalmyk princes than his father makes on silk. Find him at a nard table in the Armenian caravanserai, rolling double sixes, apologizing and rolling them again. He has won a Kalmyk saddle, a Persian falcon and a Cossack's promise not to kill him, and wants to be sent somewhere with a table worth losing at. Comic relief or a rival; his father's letters get shorter every season.

blocks.text: **Real people act as history records.** Mariana of Austria, Colbert, the Kangxi Emperor, Aurangzeb, Mukombwe: they're where the record puts them, doing what it says they did, and the party can be in the room. Three rules keep that honest. Give no real person invented words: describe what they decide, and let the record's own documents speak when you need a voice. An act history doesn't record (the Archbishop of Toledo leading an escort through Spain's gate) is the setting's call; know when you've made one. And keep the record's shape: the party can delay a confessor's fall, but nobody changes who was king. A real person makes a splendid patron, judge or obstacle, and a poor villain.

**The setting's own people** are the figures on the cover. Four are the fixtures a European game meets first, written as NPCs: give each a scene, not a speech. At home a table may play anyone, these four included; the reservation in the Contributors and License appendix governs publishing, not play.

items: **Mutapa's great artificer**, Simbarashe Moyo, who showed that lightning is magic's purest force, fought selling the devices abroad and lost. He faces a choice between his nation and his science (see Powers and Factions), and a party can be what forces it.

**Ilyanor Sael**, Lanternhall's elf: one of the high Hidden holding a shape in a Basel teaching hospital, who crossed with something of the Hidden still in the soul, and so remembers. A teacher, a licensing problem for every Church and a reason for a Physician party to exist.

**Anselme Lafrenaye**, the Gamester at Versailles, a graying French halfling with his own chair at his favored table. Versailles is still the king's pleasure house, so his table is where the court plays, not where it governs; he knows the odds on everything and a few of the corridors anyway. A Counsellor's patron, rival or model.

**Simon Horowitz**, a Kabbalist of Venice's ghetto given a book by the archangel Michael to decipher, trusting no one who promises anything two years after Sabbatai Zevi. The Envoy's example, and the Venice Job's way into the ghetto.

blocks.text: Two more, not on the cover: a Gamester and a Courtier, a couple who work as a pair, written as player characters a table can take as they are, or meet as rivals across a gaming table. They're English, in their twenties, and banned from more houses than most people have visited. Louche, loud, very funny about the English, and much better brought up than they let on.

**Kit Harrow**, Counsellor (Gamester), 24. A Cavalier baronet's daughter. Her father came home with the king in 1660 and lost the estate at hazard at the Groom Porter's inside two years. Kit learned the game to win it back, and found she was better at it than anyone she'd ever met. She never stopped. She plays in breeches because skirts catch on the table, and because the playhouses have made breeches on a woman the fashion. She does the season like a campaign: Whitehall in the winter, Tunbridge Wells for the waters and the card rooms in summer, Paris when London gets too hot, and the bear garden at Bankside when she's bored, in a borrowed coat and a borrowed accent. She keeps a pocketbook of every debt anyone owes her, including the ones she's forgiven, and she's never once been seen to count. She is owed money by two earls and a bishop. She owes it to one moneylender in Lombard Street, who is very patient, and very frightening.

**Ned Ashcombe**, Courtier (College of Verse), 26. The younger son of a Royalist colonel killed at Worcester, raised on a promise the Restoration hasn't kept. He came to Whitehall with nothing but a good leg, a better ear and a talent for lampoons. His lampoons are portraits of types, not people: the clerk who keeps his wife's miniature in his desk and his mistress's in his hat, the country squire up for the season who bets the harvest on a cockfight, the courtier so fashionable he's out of date by Tuesday. Everyone in London can sing them, and everyone is sure the next verse is about the man beside them. One got him banished from the court for a season; he spent it in Paris and came back with better French and worse habits. He fences well and insists he doesn't, which the men he lampoons find out when they come looking for him. He has fought five duels and lost none, mostly because he made his opponents laugh.

**The couple.** They met across a hazard table at the Groom Porter's, where Ned tried to cheat her and Kit let him, to see how good he was. They were married a year later in the Fleet, by a parson who asked no questions, on a bet Kit won. Ned maintains it doesn't count and has never once tried to prove it. They fight in public, in verse and in arithmetic, and the town takes sides; nobody has ever seen either of them take a side against the other.

**The act.** The Gamester never leaves her chair; the Wit never seems to be at the table at all. Kit plays, and Ned works the room: who's drunk, who's desperate, who has a wife who'd like to know where her pearls went. A couplet in his mouth is a signal to her (a rhyme on the king means the bank is weak; a line of Donne means the man on her left is cheating), and nobody in Europe listens to Ned closely enough to notice. When the house turns ugly, she counts and he ripostes, and they leave by the window. Neither of them has ever left a gaming house by the front door twice. They end most nights at dawn in St James's Park, among the king's new ducks and the clerks walking to work, with somebody else's money and nowhere in particular to be.

**Where they're banned.** The Groom Porter's, for a season; the Duke of York's apartments, for a lampoon; two *académies de jeu* in Paris, for winning; a Rhenish bishop's palace, for reasons both tell differently. Venice's Ridotto still lets them in, wearing masks like everyone else, which suits them both.

items: *As player characters,* both are 8th level, and their sheets are published separately. They're the pair for an intrigue game: Kit's Everyone's a Mark finds the tell, and Ned's Read finds who holds the power. In a fight, Kit's Big Player puts Ned where he needs to be, and her Know the Odds tells him exactly how much is left to cut.

*As NPCs,* they're the party's best friends or its worst rivals at any table in Europe (cross one of them and you've crossed both), and the people every Spymaster's Club agent would like to recruit, since no one notices who they talk to.
*As a team,* every debt is a hook. Somebody owes them; somebody they owe is losing patience.
Kit has won a Mutapan device at ombre from a drunk envoy, and has no idea what it does. Three services do, and one of them is already at her lodging.
Ned's latest lampoon names no one, and everyone at court thinks it's about them. A duke wants the author's name; the author wants the party to find out which duke.
The patient moneylender in Lombard Street has finally called Kit's debt, and he doesn't want money. He wants her to lose one game, on purpose, at the Ridotto, to a man who has never lost.

A rival offers Ned a place at court, a pension and a wife with an estate, if he'll swear the Fleet marriage was a joke. He's asked the party to find out who's paying for the offer, and he hasn't told Kit.

blocks.text: A Counsellor (Spymaster) and Wizard, about fifty, and the man nobody invites. He's a Freiherr from a corner of Franconia, and envoy to the Perpetual Diet at Regensburg for an imperial county so small that it shares one vote with a whole bench of counts. The Diet opened in 1663 and never closed, so Schleich has had five years with nothing to do, and he has filled them by going everywhere.

He is at every reception in Regensburg and Vienna, every wedding, every lying-in-state, every opera and every hunt, at the edge of every conversation that matters, holding a glass he never drinks. Three courts have licensed him as a wizard, because none of them could find a reason not to. He's damp, attentive and agreeable; he laughs a moment after everyone else; he remembers your mother's name and your debts. He writes it all down in a small green book. He is never quite rude enough to be shown the door, and he always knows which door you came in by.

**At the table.** The party meets him in every city, and he has always heard. He offers help nobody asked for, and it's always good. The table's slow discovery is that he is never wrong, and that somebody is paying for the green book: his county can't afford his coat.

items: Schleich greets the party by name in a city they arrived in that morning, and congratulates them on a job they haven't taken yet.
The green book has been stolen. Half of Vienna is relieved; the other half has started to worry about who has it now. Schleich asks the party to get it back, and to not read it.
Someone has finally poisoned Schleich, not fatally, and he wants to know who. He has a list, and it's long.
A minister offers the party a fortune to find out who Schleich reports to. The first clue is a bill for the coat.
